source.title: Data-driven effective model shows a liquid-like deep learning

record.tranche_reason: Tests how width/model complexity relates to test performance and double descent in binary-weight networks, using a different architecture and training method from V2.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. It reports width/model-complexity results relevant to V2, but its binary-weight networks do not reach zero training error, so it does not test widening beyond a zero-error interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: Appendix F reports the study's own continuous-weight network results: training error vanishes at an interpolation threshold and test error decreases again as width increases beyond it. These results bear on V2 in a two-hidden-layer, PCA-reduced MNIST setting. The recorded binary-weight results do not establish behavior beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the binary-weight complexity result, but omits the authors' continuous-weight double-descent control. Their main conclusion concerns smooth, connected deep-network weight spaces and a liquid-like interior, contrasted with a fragmented shallow-network landscape.
record.recipe_differences: Binary synapses trained with a mean-field method; the width and model-complexity studies do not use the one-hidden-layer ReLU setup specified in V2.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported width result compares deep networks with a shallow network; the double-descent result depends on binary versus continuous weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary-weight networks show decreasing test error with increasing model complexity without an established interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width can improve generalization in binary-weight networks even when training does not achieve interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-hidden-layer binary networks outperform the no-hidden-layer baseline once hidden-layer width is sufficiently large.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide hidden layers improve held-out accuracy over a linear shallow architecture in this PCA-reduced MNIST setting.

record.problems: The networks use binary weights and PCA-reduced MNIST inputs. The reported binary-weight sweeps do not reach zero training error, preventing a test of widening beyond the interpolation threshold. The main landscape analysis uses relatively small networks.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out performance under natural and random labels.

The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setup, downsampled CIFAR-10, and an explicitly verified unregularized, converged training recipe. Binary-weight sweeps do not establish post-interpolation behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Add the continuous-weight width sweep: training error reaches zero near alpha = 0.2, test error peaks there, and test error decreases with further widening. Separate the post-interpolation result relevant to V2 from the peak itself, which concerns double descent. Appendix F also reports continuous-weight double descent across parity and ten-class tasks and input dimensions from 10 to 50.
missing.locator: Appendix F; Fig. 17(a,b) and accompanying text

record.verdict_notes: Failure to reach interpolation in binary networks leaves V2 untested there; it does not justify a limits_scope verdict. Weight-space entropy and connectivity do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, zero training error, and widening beyond the width needed to reach zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance and tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: 20-h-h-10 binary-weight network
rows.size_stated: Width h varies; input dimension 20; output dimension 10
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer width and compared test performance with a shallow network.
rows.value: When hidden-layer size crosses a threshold (e.g., 10), test performance keeps improving over the shallow architecture.
rows.uncertainty: Ten independent trainings; fluctuation shown in figure, numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The paper states the qualitative trend but does not give exact accuracy values in the text. Training error is not reported for this width comparison.
rows.check: The comparison measures improvement over a network without hidden layers. The width near 10 marks an advantage over that baseline, not a zero-training-error threshold; training fit is not reported for this sweep.

rows.subject: 20-h-h-10 binary-weight network
rows.size_stated: Width h varies; input dimension 20; output dimension 10
rows.operation_detail: Varied model complexity and tracked test and training error for binary-weight networks.
rows.value: Test error keeps decreasing with model complexity; training error never reaches zero (or decreases extremely slowly).
rows.note: This does not establish behavior beyond a zero-training-error threshold: the paper reports that binary-weight networks do not reach zero training error in the tested settings.
rows.check: Binary networks improve with complexity but never establish an interpolation threshold, so this cannot measure V2's post-interpolation behavior. Training duration is 10^5 epochs, not 105. The plotted training quantity uses cross-entropy; nonzero loss alone does not establish nonzero classification error.

relationships.condition: Continuous-weight 20-h-h-10 networks on 2,000 PCA-reduced MNIST training examples, beyond the reported interpolation threshold
relationships.reason: Appendix F and Fig. 17(a,b) report vanishing training error at the test-error peak and a subsequent decrease in test error with increasing width; this verdict rests on text and a missing continuous-weight result row.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decrease in test error after training error vanished remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Binary-weight 20-h-h-10 MNIST networks in the reported width/model-complexity sweeps
reader_labels.reason: Test performance improves with width and test error decreases with model complexity, but the binary networks do not reach zero training error; rows R1 and R2 therefore do not establish the claim beyond an interpolation threshold.
